- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.4) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect bearish bias.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 1–3% on day 2–3 post-spike.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to drop; if below, tends to rise — adjust forecast to align with 30-day MA unless sentiment overrides.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates upward momentum in early days (e.g., days 1–5) when sentiment is rising; add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast values.  
- When sentiment peaks and then declines, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day after sentiment drops below 0.4.
